purpose: Fail-closed release acceptance evidence contract. Specification only; not yet wired into CI.

architecture_authority.accepted_pr_note: PR #49 accepted the compatible Laravel/PostgreSQL base decision on 2026-10-16; it does not supersede the later 2026-10-17 owner ADR.

target_stack.target_topology: One central database plus a separate database and restricted runtime role per tenant
target_stack.offline_contract: Flutter local-first SQLite and durable transactional outbox

prerequisites: Align PR #50 and all backend/security workflow definitions to the accepted PostgreSQL 17 architecture; remove MariaDB 11.4 as a target acceptance engine.

Commit and review the supported PHP 8.4/Laravel 13/Filament 5/Sanctum/stancl tenancy dependency lockfile and pass strict validation, clean install, platform checks and security audit on the same candidate SHA.
Add and execute PostgreSQL 17 real role/grant provisioning, isolation, recovery and application integration tests using disposable synthetic fixtures.
Review the evidence collector and required-check aggregator before making it a required CI check.

stale_if_any_mismatch: checkout_head_sha != report.tested_merge_sha when the workflow claims to test the PR merge result
workflow_revision_sha differs from the reviewed required workflow revision

environment_safety.adversarial_tests: Synthetic identities and fixtures; disposable environment only
environment_safety.concurrency_and_load_tests: Synthetic data and disposable environment only
environment_safety.backup_restore_tests: Synthetic backup sources and clean disposable restore target only

required_checks.name: Dependency and lockfile validation
commands: php --version
composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
composer install --no-interaction --prefer-dist --no-progress
composer check-platform-reqs
composer audit --locked --no-interaction
acceptance_oracles: composer.lock exists and matches composer.json without dependency update during CI
All required platform requirements pass
Security audit succeeds without disabling Composer security policy
Installed framework and tenancy versions match the approved target stack

required_checks.name: Canonical workbook 352 counts and deterministic SHA-256
commands: python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'
python scripts/export_workbook_for_laravel.py --validate-only
python scripts/test_canonical_workbook_contract.py
Export canonical manifest twice in clean directories and compare manifest bytes and SHA-256
acceptance_oracles: Required sheets and canonical template IDs exist
Exactly 352 entries: global=1, template=3, tenant=100, service=140, device=108
Keys are unique and valid
Dry run performs no database writes
Two clean exports have identical canonical manifest bytes and SHA-256

required_checks.name: Five-layer precedence and single-service isolation
commands: php artisan test --filter=EffectiveConfigResolverTest
php artisan test --filter=VersionedConfigWriterTest
Run canonical Laravel/Flutter parity fixtures on the exact head
acceptance_oracles: GLOBAL -> TEMPLATE -> TENANT -> SERVICE -> DEVICE precedence is exact
Only explicitly defined fields override earlier values
Missing fields remain inherited
Only the requested service row is resolved
Tenant/device mismatch is rejected server-side
Same fixture and version yields the same effective config hash

required_checks.name: Laravel clean PostgreSQL migrations, routes and auth
required_checks.environment: Disposable PostgreSQL 17 central DB plus tenant DBs
commands: Apply central migrations from an empty disposable PostgreSQL database
Apply tenant migrations from empty disposable PostgreSQL databases
php artisan route:list --path=api/v1
Run Laravel feature tests for login, session restoration, token revocation and unauthenticated/unauthorized cases
acceptance_oracles: All required migrations succeed on PostgreSQL 17 from an empty state
Laravel boots and required API routes are present
Auth/session/token positive and negative tests pass

required_checks.name: PostgreSQL 17 two-tenant provisioning and actual grants
required_checks.environment: Disposable PostgreSQL 17 only; synthetic tenant A/B
commands: php artisan test --filter=TenantProvisioningPostgresGrantsTest
Capture reviewed pg_roles, pg_database, schema/table/sequence grants and default privileges
Verify runtime/broker/migrator role attributes and PUBLIC privileges
acceptance_oracles: Provisioning is repeatable, concurrent and safely recoverable
Tenant A runtime can access A but is denied B
Tenant B runtime can access B but is denied A
Web/queue runtime has no global CREATE ROLE/CREATEDB or tenant owner privileges
Actual PostgreSQL catalogs and negative connection/read/write attempts prove least privilege

required_checks.name: Host, X-Forwarded-Host, membership, device and entitlement negatives
required_checks.environment: Disposable PostgreSQL 17 integration environment; synthetic identities
commands: Run HTTP feature tests for Host and X-Forwarded-Host cases
Run negative membership, device ownership and entitlement/subscription authorization cases
acceptance_oracles: Spoofed/ambiguous Host and forwarded-host requests fail closed
Tenant membership, active device ownership and entitlement are resolved server-side
No cross-tenant response/body or write is allowed

required_checks.name: Long-lived worker tenant context isolation
required_checks.environment: Disposable PostgreSQL 17 plus isolated synthetic cache/filesystem
commands: Run one long-lived worker against interleaved synthetic tenant A/B jobs
Inject job failure/retry and assert tenant context reset before the next job
acceptance_oracles: No DB, tenant, cache, filesystem/storage or effective-config context leaks across jobs
Context resets after success, exception, timeout and retry

required_checks.name: Flutter analysis, tests and offline SQLite atomicity
commands: flutter analyze --no-pub
flutter test --no-pub --reporter expanded
Run explicit offline sale/outbox SQLite atomicity, restart and retry tests
acceptance_oracles: Analysis and Flutter unit/widget tests pass
Local sale and outbox insert are atomic and roll back together on failure
Offline checkout does not call cloud endpoints
Pending outbox survives restart and retries correctly
Secure token/session restoration, revocation and explicit local-only mode are covered

required_checks.name: Sale/outbox replay and conflicting idempotency keys
required_checks.environment: Disposable Laravel/PostgreSQL 17 integration environment; synthetic transactions
commands: Run authenticated sync integration tests for identical replay
Run conflicting idempotency-key payload tests
Run concurrent duplicate delivery and durable acknowledgement tests
acceptance_oracles: Identical key/payload replay returns the same durable receipt without duplicate effects
Same key with different payload returns a conflict
Outbox ACK occurs only after server durable commit
Concurrent replay cannot duplicate sale/accounting effects

required_checks.name: Isolated deployment smoke
required_checks.environment: Disposable preview/staging target with synthetic credentials and data
commands: Deploy the exact tested immutable image digest to the isolated target
Run health, route, auth, tenant routing and basic transaction smoke tests
Verify deployed image digest equals the tested image digest
acceptance_oracles: Deployed revision/image exactly matches the evidence report
Health, migrations, API routes, auth and tenant-scoped transaction smoke pass
Rollback evidence is recorded

required_checks.name: Central, per-tenant and storage backup/restore
required_checks.environment: Synthetic disposable PostgreSQL 17 and storage source/restore targets
commands: Back up central DB, each tenant DB, storage/object data and required recoverable key material
Verify manifests and checksums
Restore into clean disposable targets and verify tenant boundaries, balances, config hashes and object bytes
acceptance_oracles: All required resources are in the backup manifest
Checksums verify before and after restore
Central, tenant and storage restores are successful and tenant boundaries remain intact
Restore duration and failures are recorded

required_checks.name: Performance and resource measurements
required_checks.environment: Synthetic workload in disposable environment only
commands: Run the reviewed reproducible load workload
Capture throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, CPU, peak memory, DB connections, disk/IO and storage growth
Compare the result to an owner-approved committed threshold budget
acceptance_oracles: Workload configuration and synthetic seed are reproducible
Metrics and errors are machine-readable
Threshold budget is approved and present
Measured results meet the budget with required headroom
required_checks.blocker: The ADR gives a KVM2 hardware envelope but no endpoint-specific performance thresholds; thresholds must be approved, not invented.
